title: The Final Alibi Anew
premise: Sebastian Vasquez, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has quietly unraveled three 'accidental' deaths, takes on the cold case of Marisol Reyes, a woman who vanished thirty years ago. When Marisol's recovered diary contains entries written after her disappearance—and the handwriting begins mirroring Sebastian's own—Sebastian realizes someone alive is still curating the past to protect an alibi woven three decades ago. As she digs into a 1994 fire at the Aldermoor estate that killed two people and enriched four survivors, her investigation awakens a killer who has killed before and will again. In the end, Sebastian must choose between exposing the truth and preserving the fragile new life of the woman who wrote those impossible diary entries: Marisol herself, alive, complicit, and running out of time.
about_author: Silas Nystrom is a former claims adjuster from the Pacific Northwest who spent eleven years reading other people's disasters for a living before turning them into fiction. He writes in longhand in ferry terminals, claiming the fog helps him remember what his characters would rather forget.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Deaths
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She closes her third quietly solved 'accident,' cataloguing details no one asked her to notice—the angle of a scuff mark, a teacup placed by a left hand. Her gift feels like both talent and curse. Emotional beat: competent isolation, the loneliness of seeing too much.

chapters.title: A Diary That Outlived Its Owner
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A lawyer delivers Marisol Reyes's recovered diary as evidence in a lapsed life-insurance claim. The final entry is dated eleven days after Marisol vanished in 1994. Sebastian reads it twice from memory, word-perfect, and feels the floor tilt. Beat: fascination shading into dread.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, with flashback texture. She reconstructs the Aldermoor estate fire: two dead, four survivors, a payout, silence. Each survivor built a life on the ashes. She interviews the first, retired Judge Corliss Hale, whose alibi is polished like heirloom silver. Beat: the past presenting a flawless face.

chapters.title: Handwriting Like Mine
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The late diary entries shift subtly—phrases Marisol couldn't have known, then phrases only Sebastian uses. Someone is writing to her through a dead woman's voice. She photographs every page; her memory holds it all whether she wants it or not. Beat: violation, being watched across time.

chapters.title: The Second Survivor Lies Beautifully
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Businessman Theo Brandt gives an alibi so rehearsed it has seams only memory can catch—he names a bartender who wasn't employed there until 1996. That night, someone searches Sebastian's apartment but takes nothing, leaving the diary untouched. Beat: escalation; the game has rules now.

chapters.title: Detective Okafor's Cold Files
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Detective Amara Okafor, who once dismissed Sebastian as a nuisance, reopens her own doubts about the fire. Their uneasy alliance forms over bad coffee and older lies. Okafor reveals a fourth death in 1997, ruled accidental, never insured. Beat: reluctant trust.

chapters.title: What the Fire Kept
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At the ruined Aldermoor grounds, now a vineyard, she matches scorch patterns to her memory of photographs and finds the fire started in two places. Love interest thread begins: vineyard owner Elena Marsh, the youngest survivor, watches her with grief that doesn't perform. Beat: tenderness amid suspicion.

chapters.title: Elena Remembers Differently
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. Elena recalls the night in fragments—her father's shouting, a locked study, Marisol's car still in the drive when the flames rose. She has spent thirty years not saying this aloud. Sebastian's questions feel like hands prying open a door she nailed shut. Beat: guilt and longing entwined.

chapters.title: An Alibi Thirty Years Woven
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She maps the four survivors' statements against each other and finds they corroborate one another perfectly—too perfectly, a lattice built to hold weight. One thread is fraying: Judge Hale's account changed between 1994 and 1997 depositions. Beat: the architecture of the lie becomes visible.

chapters.title: The Entry Dated Tomorrow
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A new page appears in the diary while it sits in police evidence storage, dated the coming Friday, describing Sebastian's death by drowning. Only three people had access. Okafor suspects Sebastian herself. Beat: terror weaponized; the hunter named prey.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. Elena and Sebastian circle each other over wine and withheld truths, and something real ignites despite everything Elena may be hiding. Elena begs Sebastian to drop the case—not threateningly, desperately. Duty says walk away; love says stay. Beat: the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: Marisol's Sister Speaks
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Marisol's sister, dying of illness, confesses Marisol didn't vanish—she fled, carrying proof of who set the fire, and mailed the diary back in installments ever since. The last installment arrived last month. Someone else has been intercepting them. Beat: the case inverts; the missing woman is a correspondent.

chapters.title: Theo Brandt's Last Appointment
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Theo Brandt is found dead hours before agreeing to recant his alibi—an apparent heart attack. Sebastian's memory flags the same misplaced-detail signature from her three prior cases. The killer is following her investigative rhythm, killing where she looks. Beat: horror of being predictable.

chapters.title: The Photograph Memory Trap
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian realizes her perfect recall can be used against her: the killer plants false details knowing she'll trust them. She must learn to doubt the one faculty she's built her life on. She begins keeping a paper journal—imperfect, human—as counterweight. Beat: crisis of identity.

chapters.title: Judge Hale Breaks
chapters.summary: Sebastian and Okafor POV alternating. Confronted with the deposition discrepancy, Hale admits he saw who left the study that night but took hush money to forget. He names no one before suffering a stroke that evening—poisoned, though provable to no one. Beat: truth arriving just ahead of its destruction.

chapters.title: The Fourth Survivor
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Everyone counts four survivors, but Sebastian's memory of the insurance file surfaces a fifth name, struck through: the caretaker, Daniel Voss, declared dead in the fire—no body ever confirmed. He has been the hand behind the diary pages all along, protecting someone. Beat: the shape of the enemy emerges.

chapters.title: Friday, By the Water
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The prophesied Friday arrives. Okafor stakes out the reservoir; the killer anticipates the surveillance and strikes elsewhere, taking Elena. The diary's final genuine entry, decoded, gives a location: the old Aldermoor boathouse, midnight. Beat: dread crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: Midnight at the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian walks into Voss's trap alone to buy Okafor time. Voss, the fire's true setter, has spent thirty years curating Marisol's silence and now needs one final alibi: Sebastian's death, arranged to mirror 1994 exactly. Beat: confrontation; the price of survival demanded in full.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Wrote Forward
chapters.summary: Dual POV climax. Marisol herself appears—alive, having sent the diary pages as breadcrumbs for thirty years, waiting for someone with a memory that couldn't be edited. Together they turn Voss's staged scene against him; Sebastian recites his own words back to him, word-perfect, as Okafor's lights flood the boathouse. Beat: memory as weapon; catharsis.

chapters.title: Alibis Unwoven
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The aftermath: Voss confesses in detail he believes no one could know was false—but Sebastian's testimony, corroborated by the physical record, dismantles the surviving alibis. Hale dies without naming his protector; some threads stay cut. Elena is cleared, changed, uncertain. Beat: justice imperfect but real.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian chooses not to press charges against Marisol for decades of deception, arguing survival's price was paid long ago—a decision that costs her professionally and frees her personally. She and Elena begin something unhurried among the vines. Beat: love chosen over duty, gently.

chapters.title: The Final Alibi, Anew
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV, closing frame. Marisol writes a diary entry dated today—the first honest one in thirty years—and mails it to no one. Sebastian visits, and they read the old entries together, letting memory be shared instead of hidden. The last line: some alibis are only stories we tell to survive becoming ourselves. Beat: peace earned, memory redeemed.
